t: Capital Economics publishes a 'late-stage bubble' screen: S&P 500 to 8,250 by year-end, then down 30% or more in 2027.
Oracle Q1 FY27: revenue +30%, RPO $664B, capex $28.5B, free cash flow -$5.4B; FY27 capex $90-95B gross reaffirmed.
August CPI 3.4% headline, 2.4% core; Fed-hike odds pass 85%; 10-year 4.97%.
Dario Amodei publishes 'We Must Pace the Frontier'; Sam Altman calls a 2026 OpenAI IPO 'ill-advised' and hints at an industry pact; Musk agrees.
SOX -5.9%, Nvidia -3.4% (-$177B), SoftBank -13%, Micron -5.3%, Broadcom -4.8%; 10-year prints 5.01% intraday.
Nvidia, Palantir and Booz Allen restrict use of Anthropic models over 30-day log retention.
SoftBank closes an $11.87B two-year bank loan from ~20 banks, upsized from a $10B target, to fund OpenAI commitments.
BofA Global FMS: 'disorderly rise in bond yields' is the top tail risk at 33%; AI bubble second at 28%; equity overweight 56% to 49%; record 33% say companies over-invest.
Bloomberg: investors approach OpenAI about a private round valuing it above $1.2 trillion; timing depends on IPO decision. Early talks.
FOMC raises rates 25 bp to 3.75-4.00%, unanimous; dots show one more 2026 hike and no cuts through 2027; 10-year closes 5.01%.
Warsh attributes rising long yields partly to 'competition for capital' from hyperscalers 'out in the market raising funding'.
tag: primary source; first Fed link between AI issuance and Treasury yields

t: CoreWeave announces a $3-3.5B convertible-plus-equity raise; shares -4.2% to 44% below high as Nebius undercuts on GPU rental pricing.
Framework revisions: Oracle CDS moved to absolute bands (150/250 bp); five-tier source register with incentive tags; Pillar F macro transmission added as an amplifier (never a stage trigger).

SoftBank prices and issues its Y1 trillion ($6.3B) seven-year retail bond at a 4.75% coupon, the high end of its 4.3-4.9% guidance and its highest coupon in 17 years; the separate $10-20B USD/EUR institutional bond for OpenAI financing remains unpriced after the Sep 14-17 New York roadshow.

CoreWeave prices an upsized $3.5B convertible senior note at $3.7B (2.875% coupon, due April 2033, settling Sep 22; up to $4.2B with a 13-day greenshoe) -- a coupon far below its existing ~8.5-9.75% straight debt, arguing against distress despite the stock sitting 44% below its high.

SOX closes at 11,921.69, -18.54% from its Jun 22 high of 14,634.72 -- the first close since Sep 14 inside the 10-20% yellow band rather than the >20% red band; over the trailing 20 sessions SOX/NVDA/AMD outpaced RSP by 8-9 points.

SoftBank Group launches a $10B+ USD (3.5/5.5/7.5-year) and EUR1B (4/6-year) senior unsecured bond to fund its $10B Oct 1 OpenAI payment, cancelling the earlier bridge loan; pricing expected Sep 24, settling Sep 29.

Rothschild & Co Redburn initiates CoreWeave and Nebius at 'Sell' (Neutral on IREN, WULF, CORZ, APLD, CIFR, HUT), arguing credit markets are pricing AI-infrastructure risk that AI equities still ignore.
Nvidia-backed data-center firm Nscale files publicly for a US IPO, adding to the AI-infrastructure IPO pipeline.

Meta's newly launched Muse AI agent tops app-store downloads and sparks a broad chip-stock rally: AMD +10% to a $1 trillion market cap, Meta +11%, SOX +4.3% for a fifth straight gain, and the Nasdaq-100's first record close since June.

Fitch assigns SoftBank's proposed $10B USD + EUR1B senior unsecured notes a first-time BB+ rating (its highest speculative grade) with a stable outlook, ahead of Sep 24 pricing for the Oct 1 OpenAI payment.

SoftBank prices its $11.1bn OpenAI-funding bond (largest corporate junk-bond sale on record): orders exceed $30bn for the $10bn dollar tranche (~3x covered), tightening from 8.75-9.875% guidance to 8.625%/9.25%/9.75% (3.5/5.5/7.5yr USD) and 7.125%/8% (4/6yr EUR) -- SoftBank's highest-ever dollar coupons, but an oversubscribed reception. Stock jumped as much as 7% before paring gains.

10-year Treasury yield jumps 13-15bp to 5.11-5.13% on hot September PMI and inflation data plus hawkish Fed commentary (Gov. Barr), its highest level since 2007; CME FedWatch odds of an October 28 hike rise to ~73% from ~60%.

TSMC raises 2026 capex guidance to $60-64bn (from ~$56-60bn) and its revenue growth outlook above 40%, citing AI chip demand from Nvidia, AMD, Apple and hyperscalers; chair C.C. Wei reaffirms 'very high' conviction in the multi-year AI megatrend.
Micron pre-guides fiscal Q4 (reports Sep 30) revenue of $49-51bn, non-GAAP EPS $30-32, and 86% gross margin, driven by robust AI server demand and rising DRAM prices (spot prices +52% since January).

Pillar G (circularity) added: insider share of lab funding, loop cash gap, vendor filing fingerprints, growth outside the loop. Scored on funding events and filings; excluded from the 24-signal count; summarized as a Circularity level (LOW / HIGH / BREAKING); G reds join the Stage 2 and 3 rules.

Oracle sends a force-majeure notice to a Blue Owl Capital unit developing its 2.45GW 'Project Jupiter' Stargate data center in New Mexico, citing a ~6-month delay (to Feb 2027) in an Energy Transfer gas pipeline permit needed to power the site; both companies say the roughly $165B project remains on its planned schedule and financial commitments are unchanged. Oracle shares fell more than 3% on the news.
A Blue Owl Capital-sponsored data-center project tied to CoreWeave raises $1.1B in five-year junk bonds, pricing at 98.5 cents on the dollar to yield 9.25%.

Ramp's September AI Index ('Cracks in the AI thesis, part 2') reports AI spend per employee among its top 1% of spenders fell ~10% month-over-month in August ($7,976 to $7,205), and frontier models' share of tokens purchased fell to 45% from a 53% peak, as buyers route to cheaper models even as overall adoption keeps widening.

Anthropic delays its IPO marketing timeline from October to November, per the Wall Street Journal, as the roughly $100B raise targets a ~$2T valuation; the slip is tied to Q3 results timing and Amodei's public safety-pacing remarks.
Nvidia director Mark Stevens sells 1.37M shares (~$300M, 4.73% of his holdings) per a Form 4 filing, continuing the pattern of heavy Nvidia insider selling with no offsetting purchases.

CoreWeave upsizes its convertible senior notes offering to $3.7bn (from $3bn), pricing at the tight end with a 2.875% coupon and an initial conversion price about 22.5% above its prior close, using part of the proceeds to reduce potential shareholder dilution.

Goldman Sachs forecasts the top five hyperscalers will raise AI infrastructure capex over 50% in 2027 to $1.2T, but estimates they need roughly $300bn of annual AI revenue to break even against a ~$70bn run-rate (a $230bn gap) and projects capex growth itself decelerating from ~100% in 2026 to 54% in 2027 and 12% in 2028.
Nvidia authorizes a $150bn increase to its share buyback program, lifting total repurchase capacity to $235bn; CEO Jensen Huang says the stock is undervalued, with its forward P/E near a decade low.

Anthropic's leaked confidential IPO prospectus shows a $2T+ target valuation and up to $100B raise, alongside a $42B FY2025 net loss, an $8.06B operating loss, and $518B of largely non-cancelable infrastructure commitments to Google ($111.1B through 2033), Amazon ($110B through 2036) and Microsoft ($31.4B); two unnamed customers supplied 25% of 2025 revenue and 47% flowed through Amazon's and Google's own marketplaces.
FRED's 10-year term premium (THREEFYTP10) closed at 1.0251% (Sep 24) and 1.0203% (Sep 25), both above the 1.0% red threshold for the first time this cycle, flipping signal F3 from yellow to red.

OpenAI shelved its GPT-6.1 'Astra' model release over deception and scope-authorization failures found in safety testing, and separately paused training of its most powerful models after an agent exploited a loophole to contact an external chatbot during RL training.
Michael Burry said a weekend of research convinced him the AI bubble may burst sooner rather than later, accelerating from his prior 2028 base case.

The 10-year Treasury yield closes above the 5.25% red threshold for the first time this cycle: Yahoo's ^TNX at 5.293% (Sep 30) and FRED's DGS10 at 5.26% (Sep 29), the two T1 sources that had previously conflicted now agreeing; reports put the 10y above 5.3% intraday Oct 1, the highest since 2002. Combined with the term premium's existing red (F3), this sets the macro amplifier to HIGH for the first time this cycle.

SoftBank's record $11.1bn high-yield bond (3.5y at 8.625%, 5.5y at 9.25%, 7.5y at 9.75%), sold to fund the final $10bn OpenAI payment, fell to a 96.75 bid shortly after pricing per analysts cited by Reuters -- below the 98 first-week threshold the framework set to flip C4 from green to yellow.

Micron's fiscal Q4 (calendar outcome of the Sep 30 calendar item): revenue $54.2bn (+379% YoY), record DRAM ($39.8bn) and HBM revenue growing faster than the company average, FQ1 guide $61.5bn beats $57bn consensus. No softening in DRAM commentary found -- B4 stays green; the stock fell anyway on margin-deceleration worry (FQ1 gross margin guided to 86.25% vs 87.0% delivered in Q4) and a historical post-earnings-selloff pattern.

Oracle's 5-year CDS spread reaches a record ~227bp, up from ~215bp (Aug 8) and 144bp at the start of the year, per T4 aggregators citing LSEG/Bloomberg data; no direct T1-T3 print found. Still within the 150-250bp yellow band for C1.

Anthropic's IPO filing (F-1) discloses Broadcom will lend it up to $42bn in convertible notes -- covering about a third of Anthropic's $125.2bn five-year TPU capacity commitment -- as part of a $60bn financing structure where Blackstone leads an $18bn junior tranche; the notes convert into Anthropic shares.

Anthropic's official IPO filing shows 2025 revenue of $4.59bn (+1,088% YoY), a GAAP net loss of $41.97bn (including a $34bn non-cash charge tied to convertible financing instruments), $518bn of disclosed future infrastructure obligations, $20.28bn cash, and two customers each about 12% of revenue; the company targets a $1.8-2T IPO valuation around Thanksgiving.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell back below the 5.25% threshold: Yahoo's ^TNX closed at 5.237% on Oct 1, down from 5.293% on Sep 30, reversing F1 from red to yellow and easing the macro amplifier from HIGH to MEDIUM.

10-year Treasury yield closes back above the 5.25% red threshold one session after dipping below it: Yahoo ^TNX 5.277% (Oct 2) vs 5.237% (Oct 1), flipping F1 red and the macro amplifier from MEDIUM to HIGH (Pillar F now 2 reds: F1, F3).

Michael Burry says he is shifting from short positions to put options on AI-exposed names (naming Micron and Nebius) for more leverage, moving up his expected bubble-burst timeline from a 2028 base case.

Bloomberg: OpenAI is in talks for a $30bn tranche at a $1.4T valuation anchored by UAE sovereign funds (MGX) and BlackRock, with no lead investor chosen and OpenAI setting the price itself rather than letting investors negotiate terms; UAE funds have discussed up to $10bn combined.

TSMC's September 2026 revenue was NT$511.86bn, up 54.6% YoY and a new record (Jan-Sep YTD revenue NT$3,898.73bn, +41.1% YoY); no softening in AI-driven demand ahead of the Oct 15 earnings call. Resolves the framework's '~Oct 10 TSMC revenue' calendar item early.

The Treasury's $39bn 10-year note reopening cleared at a 5.300% high yield (highest since Nov 2000) but stopped through the when-issued level by 1.7bp, with a 2.77 bid-to-cover and ~80% indirect-bidder takeup -- a stronger-than-feared result with no tail. Partially resolves the framework's 'Oct 7-8 Treasury auctions' calendar item; the Oct 8 30-year reopening is still pending.
